parsed.answer: This is a known issue. The exception (0x80263001, 'Desktop composition is disabled') is thrown when Windows' Desktop Window Manager briefly turns composition off, for example during a GPU driver reset, a display or power-state change, or a black-screen flicker like the one you saw when unplugging the charger. PowerToys Run's window then crashes and shows the 'ran into an issue' dialog. The crash is not caused by anything you did in PowerToys. The past tickets were all closed as duplicates of PowerToys#31226, which is where this problem is tracked, so you can follow it or add a thumbs-up there. The maintainers' advice in the most recent ticket was to update PowerToys to version 0.96 or later. You are on 0.83.0.0, so update first. If the blackouts and system lag continue after that, also update your GPU and graphics drivers, because the black-screen events themselves come from the display driver or power-state change rather than from PowerToys.
